title: SEI's API Platform Enables Clients' Digital Growth | SEI Developer Portal
body_text: SEI (NASDAQ:SEIC) today announced the launch of the SEI Developer Portal (the Portal), a global, self-service offering featuring SEI's suite of application programming interfaces (APIs) for web, mobile, single-page, and client/server development. The Portal supports company's strategic initiative to streamline platform integration across clients, strategic partners, and third-party technology and data providers. "We recognize that firms want to leverage their strong, in-house development expertise to build applications, yet those applications still require third-party integration. The SEI Developer Portal provides fast, flexible, and secure integration with SEI's core business services and client data, mutually reducing development timelines and expenses," said Jim Warren, Senior Vice President and Head of Platforms and Solutions for SEI's Global Wealth Management Services. "APIs areproducts, consumed by developers. Our goal is to build APIs for our customers' needs, simplifying integration in the wealth and investment management markets." The SEI Developer Portal is designed to arm developers with tools and content to integrate features and functionality across front-, middle- and back-office services using registered applications, API keys/secrets and SEI's various licensed API products. SEI has developed more than 50 API products, extending its internal business services to its client base through this new digital offering. Developers catering to the wealth and investment management markets benefit fro the API platform through improved interoperability, increased reusability, sandbox environments, and standard interfaces. Implementing a best-of-breed strategy, SEI leverages a container-based platform and automated Continuous Integration/Continuous Development (CI/CD) pipeline to help deliver minimum-viable products to the market The Portal's APIs follow RESTful design principles and are complaint with the OpenAPI specificaion, allowing SEI APIs to generate code libraries in multiple languages. About SEI After 50 years in business, SEI (NASDAQ:SEIC) remains a leading global provider of investment processing, investment management, and investment operations solutions that help corporations, financial institutions, financial advisors, and ultra-high-net-worth families create and manage wealth. As of Sept. 30, 2019, through its subsidiaries and partnerships in which the company has a significant interest, SEI manages, advises or administers $1 trillion in hedge, private equity, mutual fund and pooled or separately managed assets, including $335 billion in assets under management and $662 billion in client assets under administration. For more information, visit seic.com .

title: Kforce Inc. to Announce Second Quarter Results on July 27, 2026
FDA-Approved Second-Line Therapies for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
summary: FDA-approved second-line therapies for advanced HCC after sorafenib: regorafenib, cabozantinib, ramucirumab, pembrolizumab, and nivolumab, with indications.
body_text: FDA-approved second-line therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) Direct answer Four agents carry an FDA indication explicitly for HCC patients previously treated with sorafenib, and a fifth (nivolumab) now covers the previously-treated setting only as part of a combination regimen: Drug (brand) Class / mechanism Second-line indication wording Biomarker Regimen Application Regorafenib (Stivarga) Multikinase (VEGFR/TIE2) inhibitor HCC "previously treated with sorafenib" 30 None 30 Monotherapy (studied with best supportive care) 21 NDA 203085 231 Cabozantinib (Cabometyx) Multikinase (MET/VEGFR/AXL) inhibitor HCC "previously treated with sorafenib" 91 None 91 Monotherapy, 60 mg once daily 91 103 NDA 208692 197 Ramucirumab (Cyramza) Anti-VEGFR2 monoclonal antibody HCC with elevated AFP "treated with sorafenib" 49 50 AFP >=400 ng/mL (OCR "2400 ng/mL") 49 50 Single agent 49 BLA 125477 180 Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) Anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody HCC "previously treated with sorafenib" 58 None 58 Monotherapy 58 Accelerated approval; KEYNOTE-394 252 Nivolumab (Opdivo) + ipilimumab Anti-PD-1 + anti-CTLA-4 HCC "previously treated with sorafenib" 1 204 None Combination (nivolumab + ipilimumab) 204 206 BLA — see note below Detail by agent Regorafenib (Stivarga) The label indicates Stivarga for HCC patients "who have been previously treated with sorafenib," an explicitly second-line/previously-treated indication with no biomarker requirement 30 . The pivotal HCC study (RESORCE) administered regorafenib 160 mg once daily plus best supportive care versus placebo plus BSC, so it is used as a single oral agent rather than a biomarker-selected combination 21 . The HCC efficacy supplement under NDA 203085 was approved on 2017-04-27, and the product remains marketed (prescription) 232 231 . Cabozantinib (Cabometyx) Cabometyx is indicated "for the treatment of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who have been previously treated with sorafenib," again a previously-treated/second-line setting with no biomarker requirement 91 . It is used as monotherapy at 60 mg once daily 91 103 . The HCC efficacy supplement under NDA 208692 was approved on 2019-01-14 (CELESTIAL) and the product remains marketed 197 . Ramucirumab (Cyramza) Cyramza is the only biomarker-selected second-line HCC agent. The label indicates it "as a single agent" for HCC patients "who have an alpha fetoprotein (AFP) of [>=400] ng/mL and have been treated with sorafenib" 49 50 . This is the second-line setting restricted to AFP-high patients, based on the REACH-2 trial. The HCC efficacy supplement under BLA 125477 was approved on 2019-05-10 and the product remains marketed 180 . Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) Keytruda is indicated for HCC patients "who have been previously treated with sorafenib," as monotherapy with no stated biomarker requirement 58 . This indication originated as an accelerated approval and its confirmatory evidence is described in the label via the KEYNOTE-394 study 252 . (The specific accelerated-approval/continued-approval contingency sentence was not captured verbatim in the label pages retrieved, so that language should be confirmed against the current full label 252 .) Nivolumab (Opdivo) plus ipilimumab The nivolumab program illustrates how the second-line HCC landscape has shifted. Nivolumab originally held a monotherapy accelerated approval for HCC after sorafenib; the current label no longer presents nivolumab monotherapy as an active HCC indication and instead frames that as historical study evidence 211 217 . Current labeled use is nivolumab in combination with ipilimumab, both for first-line unresectable/metastatic HCC (CHECKMATE-9DW) 210 212 and for previously treated patients who progressed on or were intolerant to sorafenib 1 204 206 . So in the previously-treated (second-line) setting, nivolumab is now available only as the nivolumab + ipilimumab combination, not as single-agent nivolumab 211 217 . First-line agents (excluded, for context) The following systemic HCC agents are labeled for the first-line setting (no prior systemic therapy) and therefore are not second-line therapies: Sorafenib (Nexavar): indicated for unresectable HCC; the label does not require prior systemic therapy and it is the historical first-line comparator 119 120 . Lenvatinib (Lenvima): "first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable HCC"; the pivotal study enrolled patients with no prior systemic therapy 161 142 . Atezolizumab (Tecentriq) + bevacizumab: for patients "who have not received prior systemic therapy" (IMbrave150), a first-line combination 125 141 . Durvalumab (Imfinzi) + tremelimumab: for patients who "had not received prior systemic treatment for HCC" (HIMALAYA), a first-line combination 76 . Practical notes for RA reviewers The classic second-line oral TKIs (regorafenib, cabozantinib) and the AFP-selected antibody (ramucirumab) were all approved as post-sorafenib options in 2017 to 2019 and remain on the market 232 197 180 . Ramucirumab is the only second-line agent with an on-label biomarker gate (AFP), which matters for eligibility and companion-diagnostic considerations 49 50 . The checkpoint-inhibitor second-line indications were built on post-sorafenib populations, but the field is moving toward first-line immunotherapy combinations (atezolizumab+bevacizumab, durvalumab+tremelimumab, nivolumab+ipilimumab), which reshapes what "second-line" means once a patient has already received an IO-based first-line regimen 210 125 76 . "Previously treated with sorafenib" is the exact label anchor for the second-line indications; none of these labels define second-line after first-line immunotherapy, so post-IO sequencing is off-label and a reasonable follow-up question to research further.

title: AI Boom Powers Memory Chip Rally as China Gains
summary: Surging AI data-center demand lifts memory pricing and chip stocks, with China's CXMT gaining power while Nvidia, Micron and TSMC ride the wave.
body_text: Despite the record haul, Nvidia stock is up only about 12% in 2026 year to date, narrowly beating the S&P 500's roughly 12%, and trades near $208.75 at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 23.6, roughly a 10% premium to the index. That is a modest premium against a track record of annual returns of 39% in 2025, 171% in 2024, 239% in 2023, and 978% since late July 2021. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress framed the runway in her outlook: "AI infrastructure spending is on track to reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion annually by the end of this decade." Nvidia's 9.3% Nebius Stake Sends Cloud Stock Up 19% Nvidia is also spreading its capital across the AI supply chain. As reported by The Motley Fool , Nvidia disclosed a 9.3% equity stake in cloud-computing company Nebius, sending Nebius stock up nearly 19% on Tuesday to trade near $221.43, above Nvidia's own price near $208.76. Rounding out the group, Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) , described by The Motley Fool as "arguably the best manufacturing company in the world," slipped about 1.42% (roughly $6.00) on July 21, 2026. The pullback in the world's largest contract chipmaker, alongside minor moves in Nvidia and Micron, sits against a backdrop of demand that both US leaders and Chinese challengers are racing to serve. body_text: NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION TO UNITED STATES NEWSWIRE SERVICES OR FOR DISSEMINATION IN THE UNITED STATES Obsidian Energy Announces $75 million Add-On to our Existing Senior Unsecured Notes Calgary, Alberta–(Newsfile Corp. – July 15, 2026) – OBSIDIAN ENERGY LTD. (TSX: OBE) (NYSE American: OBE) (“ Obsidian Energy “, the “ Company “, “ we “, “ us ” or “ our “) announces that we have entered into an underwriting agreement to sell, on a private placement basis (the “ Offering “), an additional $75.0 million aggregate principal amount to our existing 8.125% senior unsecured notes due December 3, 2030, issued on December 3, 2025 (the “ Notes “). title: Important Changes for Shipping to the EU Starting July 1, 2026
summary: EasyPost - Important Changes for Shipping to the EU Starting July 1, 2026 %
body_text: Starting July 1, 2026, the European Union is eliminating the de minimis duty threshold for imported goods. This means all shipments to the EU will now be subject to import duties, regardless of value. As a result, several EU member states will stop accepting Delivered Duty Unpaid (DDU) shipments, meaning packages without prepaid duties may be refused, returned, or subject to higher handling fees at destination. These changes affect anyone importing to EU countries. EasyPost strongly recommends taking action ahead of peak season to ensure that packages reach their destinations on time without incurring extra fees. What exactly is changing? On July 1, 2026: The EU de minimis threshold is removed for all goods. A temporary €3 flat-rate duty per commodity/HS code takes effect.* Duties are non-refundable, even if the package is not delivered. DDU shipments will not be accepted by several EU countries, and countries that do accept them will apply a higher handling fee (€15–€25) that will increase the likelihood of customer refusals and returns. In the future: A separate EU-wide handling fee, reported at roughly €2 per shipment, has been proposed for November 1, 2026, but is not yet finalized in the released regulation. Full ad valorem (percentage-based) duties are expected in 2028. *Note: The EU’s Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) system does not support the new €3 flat-rate duty. IOSS shippers will need a separate solution, such as DDP, to cover this charge. What you should do as a shipper To keep shipping costs low and avoid an increase in returned products, EasyPost recommends making these three changes as soon as possible: Transition to Delivered Duty Paid (DDP): Prepay duties and taxes at the time of shipment with DDP to avoid high handling fees and ensure smooth customs clearance. Prepare to share your Product Identifiers (PIDs): This refers to the merchant SKU, the manufacturer’s own product code, and the standardized GTIN/EAN/UPC where one exists. Including the PID is voluntary from July 1, but mandatory starting November 1, 2026. Consult with carriers: Contact your carriers for guidance, and consider adding new carriers to your mix. Carrier FAQ USPS USPS PC Postage does not support DDP today. USPS Ship supports DDP via shipment.options.incoterms=DDP. If you’re currently importing with EasyPost’s USPS account (PC Postage), you’ll want to add USPS Ship to your carrier mix use their DDP service. FedEx Starting November 1, 2026, FedEx will require shippers to complete the PID field. We recommend FedEx shippers select “Bill Shipper” for their DDP packages to ensure duties and taxes are not invoiced to the recipient. UPS UPS® Worldwide Economy DDU services to Germany will be suspended. Asendia Supports shippers who need to use DDU temporarily or are just entering the EU market. Duties are calculated and handled earlier in the shipping journey but after checkout. DHL DHL supports DDP under “Duties and Taxes Paid (DTP)”. Through EasyPost, this is enabled via options.incoterm = “DDP”. Starting July 1, 2026, DHL Express will require a signed Power of Attorney, attestation letter, and line-item data (buyer, seller, retail value) per shipment. Mixed-value shipments will lose consolidated clearance benefits. With these changes taking effect on July 1, 2026 , we recommend contacting your account team or integrating with DDP solutions as soon as possible.

title: Best Places to Visit in India in August 2026 (Monsoon Travel Guide)
summary: 12 best places to visit in india in august 2026 grouped by monsoon effect: destinations made better by rain, rain-free zones, off-season steals, and festival travel.
body_text: The Jog Falls in January is a rock face with a trickle of water. In August, it is a 253 metre wall of white roaring loud enough to drown out conversation from 500 metres away. That difference is the entire argument for travelling in monsoon season. The places to visit in india in august are not the same destinations marketed in October brochures with the word “rain” added as a warning. They are fundamentally different versions of the same geography. This guide groups 12 destinations by what the monsoon actually does to them rather than by region. Destinations where rain creates the experience come first. Rain-free zones follow for travellers who want August weather without August water. Off-season destinations where monsoon drops prices come next. And festival-linked destinations close the list for travellers who want culture alongside climate. Places to Visit in India in August: 12 Destinations Sorted by What the Rain Does to Them Six spots across India reach their visual and experiential peak in August specifically because of rainfall. These are not destinations that “survive” the monsoon. They require it. Cherrapunji and Mawsynram, Meghalaya Meghalaya means “the abode of clouds,” and August is when the name earns itself. Cherrapunji (Sohra) and Mawsynram compete annually for the title of wettest place on Earth, and August sits in the middle of their heaviest rainfall window. The living root bridges at Nongriat, grown over decades by the Khasi tribe from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees, are at their most dramatic when waterfalls cascade directly beside them. Nohkalikai Falls, India’s tallest plunge waterfall at 340 metres, runs at maximum volume. The double-decker root bridge trek (approximately 3,500 steps each way from Tyrna village) is strenuous but manageable for fit travellers who prepare for wet, slippery stone steps. Temperature: 15 to 22 degrees Celsius | Rainfall: Heavy to extremely heavy (plan indoor backup days) How to reach: Fly to Guwahati, then 4 to 5 hour drive to Cherrapunji. Buses from Guwahati to Shillong (3 hours), then Shillong to Cherrapunji (2 hours). Best for: Waterfall chasers, trek-ready travellers, photographers who want monsoon at its most extreme Valley of Flowers, Uttarakhand The Valley of Flowers National Park opens for a limited season each year (typically June to October), and the alpine bloom peaks between mid-July and mid-August. Over 600 species of wildflowers, including the Brahma Kamal, Himalayan blue poppy, and cobra lily, carpet the valley floor at an altitude of 3,658 metres. The trek starts from Govindghat, proceeds to Ghangaria (13 km base camp), and then covers 4 km into the valley. No overnight camping is permitted inside the park. This is one of the most time-sensitive places to visit in india in august because the bloom window is narrow and weather-dependent. Temperature: 7 to 15 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Moderate (rain gear essential) How to reach: Fly to Jolly Grant Airport Dehradun, then drive to Govindghat (10 to 12 hours via Joshimath). Alternatively, bus from Rishikesh to Joshimath (10 hours), then shared taxi to Govindghat. Best for: Trekkers, botanists, and anyone who wants to see a UNESCO site at its biological peak Coorg (Kodagu), Karnataka Coffee plantations in Coorg smell different in August. The monsoon triggers a second flush of coffee blossoms, and the mist that wraps around the Kodagu hills makes Abbey Falls, Iruppu Falls, and Mallalli Falls reach their most photogenic flow. Coorg works for families, couples, and solo travellers because the experience is layered: plantation stays with home-cooked Kodava cuisine, short waterfall treks, the Nagarhole National Park fringe for wildlife, and Tibetan settlements at Bylakuppe. The monsoon getaways near Bangalore guide covers the Bangalore to Coorg bus route and a full monsoon itinerary. Temperature: 15 to 25 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Heavy How to reach: Bangalore to Madikeri buses take 5 to 6 hours. Best for: Plantation stays, waterfall treks, families wanting a green escape from Bangalore Munnar, Kerala Munnar’s tea plantations turn an electric green in August that no filter can replicate. The Western Ghats hill station sits at 1,600 metres and receives consistent rainfall through the month, which keeps temperatures between 18 and 25 degrees Celsius. Eravikulam National Park (home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr) offers walking trails when weather permits. Attukad Falls and Lakkam Falls run at full force. The Tea Museum provides a 2-hour structured introduction to the region’s plantation economy. Off-season room rates drop 30 to 50 percent compared to the December to February peak, making August one of the best-value months to visit. The Kerala monsoon travel guide covers Munnar alongside Wayanad, Alleppey, and Athirapally. Temperature: 18 to 25 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Moderate to heavy How to reach: Fly to Cochin, then 3 hours by road. Best for: Tea estate walks, monsoon photography, budget stays, couples and solo travellers Wayanad, Kerala Wayanad sits in the northern Western Ghats of Kerala and peaks in August with dense spice plantation greenery, full-force waterfalls (Soochipara, Meenmutty), and mist-covered mornings. Edakkal Caves, with 6,000-year-old petroglyphs, add a history layer. Pookode Lake offers calm boating when heavier rain pushes visitors off trekking trails. The drive through Thamarassery Ghat, with its nine hairpin bends and constant waterfall views, is a monsoon drive worth doing slowly. Temperature: 20 to 28 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Heavy How to reach: Calicut airport is 90 km away. Bangalore to Wayanad buses take 6 to 7 hours. Best for: Eco-tourism, spice plantation walks, cave history, families and nature photographers Lonavala and the Western Ghats, Maharashtra The Mumbai-Pune corridor transforms in August. Bhushi Dam overflows (the main monsoon attraction at Lonavala), seasonal waterfalls appear on every cliff face along the expressway, and Rajmachi Fort trek becomes a cloud-walking experience. Tamhini Ghat, Malshej Ghat, and Bhandardara all peak during this month. The Pune monsoon road trips guide covers the best rainy-season routes from Pune with zingbus connections. Temperature: 20 to 28 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Heavy How to reach: Mumbai to Lonavala by bus in 1.5 to 2 hours. Best for: Waterfall chasers, fort trekkers, and weekend monsoon escapes from Mumbai and Pune Where Rain Stays Away: The Clear Sky Alternatives Two destinations in India receive minimal monsoon rainfall because they sit in Himalayan rain-shadow zones. These are the places to visit in india in august for travellers who want warm days, clear skies, and landscapes that look nothing like the rest of the country in this season. Ladakh Ladakh sits behind the Great Himalayan Range, which blocks the monsoon clouds before they can cross. August temperatures in Leh range from 10 to 25 degrees Celsius under clear blue skies, while the rest of India receives heavy rainfall. Pangong Tso, Nubra Valley, Magnetic Hill, Hemis Monastery, and Khardung La are all accessible during this month. August also hosts the Ladakh Festival, a multi-day cultural celebration with masked dances, archery, and polo. The high-altitude acclimatisation requirement is real: spend at least 2 days in Leh before attempting any passes above 4,000 metres. Altitude sickness affects a significant percentage of travellers who ignore this step. Temperature: 10 to 25 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Minimal (occasional light showers) How to reach: Fly to Leh (direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Srinagar). The Manali to Leh highway is open in August (2-day drive, requires acclimatisation stops). Best for: Mountain landscape photography, monastery visits, road trips, altitude trekking, cultural festivals Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh Spiti sits at 3,800 metres average elevation in another rain-shadow pocket. The Kunzum Pass (open June to October) connects Spiti to the rest of Himachal, and August offers the widest travel window before winter closes the roads. Key Monastery (1,000+ years old, perched on a cliff at 4,166 metres), Chandratal Lake, Pin Valley National Park, and Dhankar Monastery define the itinerary. The barren, lunar landscape of Spiti is the visual opposite of every other August destination on this list: brown rock, blue sky, zero vegetation, absolute quiet. Temperature: 5 to 20 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Very minimal How to reach: Manali to Kaza takes 10 to 12 hours by road via Kunzum Pass. Shimla to Kaza via Kinnaur takes 2 days. Best for: Adventure road trips, Buddhist heritage, solitude seekers, photographers who want a desert-in-the-sky aesthetic Where Monsoon Drops Prices: Off-Season Travel Goa Goa receives heavy monsoon rainfall in August, which clears the beaches of tourist crowds and drops hotel rates by 40 to 60 percent. The experience is different: instead of sunbathing and water sports, August Goa offers the Sao Joao festival (feast of St. John, celebrated with jumping into wells and rivers), Dudhsagar Falls at peak flow, spice plantation tours in the green interior, and seafood at local restaurants without the tourist-season markup. Beach shacks close during monsoon, but indoor restaurants remain open. South Goa (Palolem, Agonda, Cola Beach) offers quieter rain-soaked beauty. Temperature: 25 to 30 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Heavy How to reach: Fly to Dabolim Airport. Mumbai to Goa overnight buses take 10 hours. Best for: Budget travellers, couples seeking off-season privacy, festival experiences, monsoon waterfall visits Udaipur, Rajasthan Udaipur in August is Udaipur at its most romantic. The lakes (Pichola, Fateh Sagar, Udai Sagar) fill to capacity, the surrounding Aravalli hills turn green, and the palace reflections in rain-rippled water photograph differently from any other season. Hotel rates drop 30 to 40 percent from the October to March peak. Monsoon Palace (Sajjangarh) earns its name during this month: the view of clouds rolling into the Aravalli valley from the hilltop is the specific reason the palace was built there. Temperature: 25 to 35 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Moderate How to reach: Fly to Udaipur Airport. Delhi to Udaipur overnight buses take 10 to 14 hours. Jaipur to Udaipur takes 6 to 7 hours. Best for: Couples, palace architecture, lake photography, budget luxury stays at off-season rates Where August Brings Festivals Alleppey (Alappuzha), Kerala August in Alleppey builds toward Onam, Kerala’s harvest festival, typically falling in late August or early September. The week leading up to Onam features Vallam Kali (snake boat races) on the backwaters, with the Nehru Trophy Boat Race being the most famous. Houseboat cruises through the rain-swollen backwaters, Ayurvedic spa treatments (the humid monsoon climate is traditionally considered the ideal season for Panchakarma therapies), and village walks along the canal network define the trip. This is one of the most culturally rich places to visit in india in august because the festival layers onto the monsoon landscape. Temperature: 25 to 30 degrees Celsius Rainfall: Moderate to heavy How to reach: Cochin airport is 53 km away. Trains from Ernakulam to Alleppey take 1.5 hours. Best for: Backwater houseboats, Ayurveda stays, snake boat race spectating, slow cultural travel You Might Also Like Monsoon Getaways Near Bangalore by Bus — Coorg, Chikmagalur, Wayanad, Dandeli, and Jog Falls with bus routes and monsoon-specific itineraries from Bangalore. Kerala Monsoon Travel Guide — Munnar, Wayanad, Athirapally, Alleppey, and the full Kerala monsoon circuit with safety tips and seasonal timing. Waterfalls Near Chennai for Day Trips — Seasonal waterfall picks near Chennai including Tada Falls, Hogenakkal, and other monsoon cascades. What August Travellers Learn the Expensive Way Waterproof your bag, not just yourself. A rain jacket keeps you dry. A dry bag inside your backpack keeps your phone, passport, and clothes dry. Wet electronics and wet documents create real problems; wet hair does not. Book hill station stays midweek. August weekends at Munnar, Lonavala, and Coorg fill up fast because they serve as monsoon escapes for the nearest metro city. A Wednesday to Friday trip to any of these destinations cuts accommodation costs and crowd levels by half. Leeches are real in the Western Ghats. Coorg, Wayanad, Chikmagalur, and Lonavala monsoon treks involve leeches on forest trails. Leech socks (available at local shops for Rs 100 to Rs 200) and salt in a zip-lock bag are the standard precautions experienced monsoon trekkers carry. Check road conditions before Spiti and Ladakh drives. Both destinations are accessible in August, but landslides on high-altitude roads can cause delays of hours or days. Follow BRO (Border Roads Organisation) updates and plan buffer days in the itinerary. Carry offline maps and downloaded tickets. Network coverage drops in Meghalaya’s interior, Spiti Valley, Ladakh’s passes, and the Western Ghats during heavy rain. Offline Google Maps, screenshots of bus tickets, and hotel booking confirmations save recovery time when signals disappear. For intercity bus travel during monsoon, check routes and live schedules on the zingbus app . GPS tracking on every departure lets family members follow the journey in real time regardless of weather. Note: Prices, timings, and conditions are approximate and may change based on season, demand, weather, and local regulations. The Month When India Shows You What It Actually Looks Like The places to visit in india in august do not compete with the October-to-March calendar. They replace it. A waterfall at 10 percent capacity is a tourist photo. A waterfall at 100 percent capacity is a natural event. A tea plantation under clear sky is scenic. A tea plantation under rolling mist with rain beading on every leaf is an experience that rewires how you think about green. August travel in India asks for waterproof shoes instead of sunscreen, flexibility instead of a fixed itinerary, and the willingness to get rained on occasionally. What it gives back is the country at a resolution no dry month can match. Frequently Asked Questions What Are the Best Places to Visit in India in August? The best places to visit in india in august include Ladakh and Spiti Valley (rain-free high altitude), Munnar and Wayanad (monsoon-green tea plantations), Coorg (coffee and waterfalls), Cherrapunji and Meghalaya (extreme rainfall and living root bridges), Valley of Flowers (alpine bloom peak), Goa (off-season prices), Udaipur (full lakes and green Aravallis), and Alleppey (Onam and backwater cruises). Is It Safe to Travel in India in August? Travelling in India in August is generally safe with proper planning. Hill stations, rain-shadow destinations like Ladakh and Spiti, and most cities function normally. Avoid flood-prone river areas and check road conditions for mountain routes. Carry waterproof gear, travel with GPS-tracked bus services, and maintain flexibility in schedules for weather-related delays. Which Places in India Have No Rain in August? Ladakh and Spiti Valley are the two primary destinations in India that receive minimal to no rainfall in August. Both sit in Himalayan rain-shadow zones where monsoon clouds cannot cross the mountain barriers. Temperatures are pleasant (10 to 25 degrees in Ladakh), skies remain clear, and roads are open for travel. Is August a Good Time to Visit Kerala? August is an excellent time to visit Kerala for monsoon-specific experiences: Ayurvedic treatments (traditionally the ideal season for Panchakarma), backwater houseboat cruises through rain-swollen canals, waterfalls at peak flow (Athirapally, Soochipara), and the build-up to Onam festival. Off-season rates on hotels and houseboats drop 30 to 50 percent. Can You Trek to Valley of Flowers in August? Yes, August is one of the best months to trek to Valley of Flowers in Uttarakhand. The alpine bloom peaks between mid-July and mid-August, with over 600 species of wildflowers visible. The park is open, the 4 km trail from Ghangaria is accessible, and the Brahma Kamal and Himalayan blue poppy are in full bloom during this window. Rain gear is essential. Is Goa Worth Visiting in August? Goa in August is worth visiting for budget-conscious travellers and monsoon lovers. Hotel rates drop 40 to 60 percent, tourist crowds disappear, Dudhsagar Falls reaches peak flow, and the Sao Joao festival adds a cultural layer. Beach shacks close, but indoor restaurants, spice plantations, and the green Goan interior offer a different kind of trip. What Should You Pack for August Travel in India? For August travel in India, pack a light waterproof jacket, quick-dry clothing, waterproof bag or dry bag for electronics, leech socks for Western Ghats treks, a power bank, offline maps, insect repellent, comfortable waterproof footwear, a light fleece for hill stations, and an umbrella. Avoid heavy cotton clothing that stays wet for hours. Is Ladakh Accessible in August? Yes, Ladakh is fully accessible in August. Flights to Leh operate daily from Delhi, Mumbai, and Srinagar. The Manali to Leh highway is open (2-day drive). Pangong Tso, Nubra Valley, Khardung La, and all major attractions are accessible. Spend at least 2 days acclimatising in Leh before attempting high passes above 4,000 metres. What Festivals Happen in India in August? Major festivals in India during August include Raksha Bandhan (celebration of sibling bonds, nationwide), Janmashtami (Lord Krishna’s birth, nationwide with major celebrations in Mathura and Vrindavan), the Ladakh Festival (multi-day cultural celebration in Leh), and the Nehru Trophy Boat Race in Alleppey leading into Kerala’s Onam festival. Are Hotels Cheaper in India in August? Hotels across most Indian tourist destinations are cheaper in August by 20 to 60 percent compared to the October to March peak season. Goa, Rajasthan, Kerala, and hill stations in South India show the steepest off-season discounts. Ladakh and Spiti are exceptions since August is their peak season and prices are at their highest. Can You Do a Road Trip in Spiti Valley in August? Yes, the Kunzum Pass connecting Spiti Valley to the rest of Himachal Pradesh is typically open from June to October, making August a viable road trip month. The Manali to Kaza route takes 10 to 12 hours. The Shimla to Kaza route via Kinnaur takes 2 days. Carry extra fuel, food, and warm clothing. Check BRO road condition updates daily since landslides can cause temporary closures. What Are the Best Monsoon Waterfalls in India to Visit in August? The best monsoon waterfalls in India in August include Jog Falls in Karnataka (253 metres, peak flow), Nohkalikai Falls in Meghalaya (340 metres, India’s tallest plunge waterfall), Dudhsagar Falls in Goa (310 metres, best accessed via trek or jeep), Athirapally Falls in Kerala (80 feet, nicknamed Niagara of India), and Abbey Falls in Coorg (70 feet, surrounded by coffee plantations). Is It Possible to Visit Udaipur in Monsoon? Udaipur is one of the most rewarding monsoon destinations in Rajasthan. August fills all five lakes to capacity, turns the Aravalli hills green, and drops hotel rates significantly. Monsoon Palace (Sajjangarh) offers dramatic cloud views, and the rain-rippled reflections of City Palace in Lake Pichola create a scene unlike any other season. How Should You Plan an August Trip in India? Plan an August trip in India by choosing the destination based on what you want from the monsoon: waterfall treks (Meghalaya, Coorg), green hill stations (Munnar, Wayanad), rain-free landscapes (Ladakh, Spiti), off-season value (Goa, Udaipur), or cultural festivals (Alleppey). Book accommodation midweek for lower rates, carry waterproof gear, keep schedules flexible, and check road and weather conditions 48 hours before departure.

title: Pizza Ranch Selects NCR Voyix to Power Next-Generation Restaurant Operations Across Its System
summary: Leading Midwest restaurant brand to deploy NCR Voyix platform, including Aloha Next, Voyix Pay and services, to support faster innovation, stronger operational consistency and long-term growth
body_text: Leading Midwest restaurant brand to deploy NCR Voyix platform, including Aloha Next, Voyix Pay and services, to support faster innovation, stronger operational consistency and long-term growth ATLANTA — July 7, 2026 — NCR Voyix (NYSE: VYX), a platform-powered leader in unified commerce for shopping and dining, today announced an exclusive platform agreement with Pizza Ranch Inc., a leading restaurant chain known for its family-friendly dining experience and franchise network across the United States. Under the agreement, NCR Voyix will serve as Pizza Ranch’s exclusive point-of-sale technology partner across corporate-owned restaurants and franchisee locations. Pizza Ranch will deploy Aloha Next, NCR Voyix’s next-generation restaurant platform built on a microservices architecture, creating a unified foundation for point of sale, payments and in-store capabilities. The platform simplifies execution, supports enterprise scalability and enables Pizza Ranch to accelerate innovation around the priorities that matter most to its operators, franchisees and customers. "We look forward to rolling out NCR Voyix's Aloha Next POS across Pizza Ranch starting in 2027. body_text: Reese Brown Junior Associate, Communications July 07, 2026 Volunteer Spotlight- Kinston Team (Habitat for Humanity) At West, our commitment to the community goes beyond our day-to-day work. Opportunities like this not only support families in need but also strengthen connections within our own teams. “When we show up and build together, we’re not just constructing homes: we’re strengthening communities,” said Kayla Homar, Sr. HR Business Partner. Thank you to the Kinston volunteers for representing West and making a meaningful change in our local community. title: Hello, assistant-ui
summary: assistant-ui is an open-source AI chat component for React.
body_text: After spending the last two years building Gen-AI prototypes and products, I realized that all software will soon have a natural language interface. OpenAI's ChatGPT sets the quality bar high and I wanted to have a similar UX in my own apps. No solution on the market came anywhere close, so I built assistant-ui. assistant-ui is an open-source, embeddable, customizable AI chat component for React web apps. You can use it to build GPT wrappers, in-app copilots, or agentic systems. It supports rich content (markdown, code highlighting, charts, tables), generative UI, message editing, ..., across all the major model providers. Earlier last month, I released the project to the world. The feedback from early adopters has been overwhelmingly positive: @raw_works i needed this 7 months ago! @eliasdevs I was able to get it into production in 2 hours @manuuonly was just thinking of researching a tool that could help me do this. awesome, great product! It didn't take long for developers to start building with assistant-ui. Here are some of my favorite products from the community: Helicone - open-source LLM observability platform screenpipe - AI to remember everything you see, say or hear myresume.guru - AI resume optimizer to land your dream job With 250+ stars on GitHub and over 1k npm weekly downloads, we got a vibrant growing community of developers who care about the user experience. I want to thank the following contributors who got the project to where it is today: @m13v for contributing two examples and several how-to videos @okisdev for multiple bugfixes @Rajaniraiyn for improving streaming support for REST APIs @ccbkai for integrating Chrome's window.ai with assistant-ui @stingfeng for building a Dify integration @Ephibbs for building a Perplexity-style text streaming library ( Demo ) … and so many others assistant-ui builds on top of Radix UI , Tailwind , shadcn/ui , Vercel AI SDK and other amazing open-source projects. Over the coming month, I'll be rolling out multimodal support, so you can use your voice and upload images. There's so much more in the pipeline that I can't wait to unveil! Today, several companies like Helicone (YC W23) are using assistant-ui to power a core part of their product. If your company wants to do the same, please get in touch . If you're building conversational AI, join us on Discord . If you're technical and want to shape how we interact with AIs of the future, send me an email .

title: I’m 62 With $850k and a Small Pension. Claiming Social Security Now Costs More Than I Thought.
summary: Claiming Social Security early at 62 can cost more over a lifetime than waiting. Here's what you need to calculate before you claim.
body_text: If you are close to retirement with a nest egg of $850,000 and a small pension, claiming Social Security early may make sense. However, claiming benefits as soon as you become eligible at age 62 will permanently reduce your monthly income. This can add up to a loss over the lifetime of your retirement. What Claiming at 62 Could Cost Someone born in 1960 or later has a full retirement age of 67 . Claiming at 62 means starting benefits five years early, which reduces the monthly benefit to 70% of the full amount, a permanent 30% reduction. 1 For context, the average Social Security retirement benefit was about $2,071 per month as of January 2026. 2 To show how claiming early could affect your benefits, let’s use that average as an example for a retiree who qualifies for a $2,071 monthly benefit at their full retirement age of 67. Claiming at 62 would reduce that amount to approximately 70% of the full benefit: Category Amount Monthly benefit at 67 $2,071 Reduction for claiming at 62 30% Dollar reduction $2,071 × 30% = $621.30 Monthly benefit at 62 $2,071 − $621.30 = $1,449.70 Annual benefit at 62 $1,449.70 × 12 = $17,396.40 Annual benefit at 67 $2,071 × 12 = $24,852 In this example, waiting until 67 would produce an additional $621.30 per month, or approximately $7,455.60 per year. On a retirement that lasts to age 85, the difference would look like this before cost-of-living adjustments and taxes: Category Amount Claim at 62 $17,396.40 × 23 years = $400,117.20 Claim at 67 $24,852 × 18 years = $447,336 Additional lifetime benefits from waiting $447,336 − $400,117.20 = $47,218.80 The retiree who waits receives checks for fewer years, but each check is permanently larger. Claiming later may only work when savings and pension income can cover the five-year income gap. A financial advisor could help you estimate how much you’d receive at different claiming ages and decide whether you should use savings to bridge the gap for a larger claim. Using Savings to Bridge the Social Security Age Gap Since claiming later means going without Social Security income for five more years, one option may be to draw more heavily from the $850,000 portfolio during that stretch. This effectively uses savings as a bridge until the larger benefit becomes available at 67. Assuming the small pension covers part of your retirement expenses, here’s an example that leaves a $24,000 annual gap: Category Amount Annual amount needed from savings $24,000 Length of bridge Five years Total portfolio withdrawals $24,000 × 5 = $120,000 This example does not include investment returns , taxes or inflation. It does, however, show how a retiree would need to use approximately $120,000 of savings as a bridge for five years until they could claim a larger Social Security benefit. To decide if the five-year bridge is worth the money, you may want to estimate a break-even age that compares how benefits would have been collected between ages 62 and 67 to the additional income gained by waiting. Category Amount Benefits that would be received from 62 through 66 $20,160 × 5 = $100,800 Additional annual benefit after 67 $8,640 Estimated time needed to recover forgone benefits $100,800 ÷ $8,640 = 11.7 years Since that 11.7-year recovery period starts at age 67, when the larger benefit begins, waiting could pay off around age 79 (67 + 11.7 years). Living beyond that point would favor delaying, but a shorter lifespan may favor claiming sooner. Taxes, investment performance and cost-of-living adjustments could change this example. When Claiming Early Could Make Sense Claiming at 62 could make sense in situations with health concerns, shorter lifespan expectations, or immediate income needs. A pension may help you delay Social Security, but payments and withdrawals from tax-deferred accounts can raise taxable income and potentially make part of the Social Security benefit taxable as well. Calculating a break-even age could help you estimate when delaying may start paying off. A financial advisor can work with you to factor in taxes and investment growth based on your Social Security estimate, tax situation and portfolio performance. Photo credit: ©iStock.com/Hispanolistic, ©iStock.com/yongyuan. Article Sources All articles are reviewed and updated by SmartAsset’s fact-checkers for accuracy. Visit our Editorial Policy for more details on our overall journalistic standards. Social Security Administration, “Benefits Planner: Retirement | Born in 1960 or later” (a wage earner who starts benefits at age 62 receives 70.0% of their full retirement benefit). https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/retirement/planner/1960.html . Social Security Administration, “What is the average monthly benefit for a retired worker?” (estimated average monthly benefit of $2,071 for January 2026). https://www.ssa.gov/faqs/en/questions/KA-01903.html . title: Treasury Prime Partners with People Trust to Advance Financial Inclusion via Embedded Banking
summary: First credit union to join Treasury Prime’s Bank Network highlights growing interest in fintech modernization among mission-driven institutions
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO, June 10, 2025 – Treasury Prime , a leading embedded banking software company, announced today that People Trust Community FCU , a mission-driven financial institution based in North Little Rock, Arkansas, has joined the Treasury Prime Network. As Treasury Prime’s first credit union partner, this milestone is a pivotal step in expanding access to embedded banking for community-based institutions. Founded to serve underbanked communities in Arkansas, People Trust is leveraging Treasury Prime’s platform to modernize its core banking services. This partnership also includes the possibility for future use of Treasury Prime’s front-end solution to replace the institution’s legacy online banking interface, enhancing member experience and increasing operational efficiency. “Modern banking isn’t just for the biggest institutions, it’s for everyone,” said Arlo Washington, founder and CEO of People Trust Community FCU. “By partnering with Treasury Prime, we’re bringing fintech-grade infrastructure to our credit union, not to chase trends, but to expand access and opportunity for the communities we serve. This is what it looks like when innovation is built on purpose.” By adopting Treasury Prime’s infrastructure, People Trust is doubling down on its mission to deliver accessible, modern financial services to low- and moderate-income communities, while also exploring fintech collaboration as a strategic path to diversify revenue, grow deposits, and expand its digital reach. “This partnership represents a turning point for community-focused institutions looking to modernize and expand through embedded banking,” said Jeff Nowicki, chief banking officer at Treasury Prime. “People Trust is leading the way for a new generation of credit unions that recognize the need to innovate without compromising their community values. Together, we’re paving the way for scalable, inclusive financial innovation.” As the first credit union in Treasury Prime’s expanding network, the addition of People Trust underscores the growing demand among community institutions for modern, embedded banking solutions. Treasury Prime’s direct-to-bank model gives institutions like People Trust the tools to compete with larger institutions, without requiring them to build complex technology stacks in-house. For more information about Treasury Prime’s end-to-end bank operating system and bank network, visit www.treasuryprime.com . To learn more about People Trust Community Federal Credit Union, visit www.ptcfcu.org . ‍ About Treasury Prime Treasury Prime is building the future of finance. Through its cutting-edge embedded banking software, Treasury Prime facilitates seamless connections between banks and enterprise partners, equipping them with everything they need to launch innovative financial products with a strong commitment to responsible practices. Beyond its core banking offerings, which encompass accounts and payment infrastructure, Treasury Prime also provides a robust partner marketplace. This marketplace offers a wide range of auxiliary services tailored to meet the diverse needs of bank-fintech partnerships. Treasury Prime was named Best Banking-as-a-Service Platform in the Tearsheet Embedded Awards 2021 and 2022, and was named to CB Insights' annual 2021 Fintech 250 list. title: Squeegee Blades 101
summary: Squeegee maintenance is an important component of clean, safe floors in your facility. Ensure you’re properly caring for your cleaning machine's squeegee blades with our squeegee maintenance tips.
body_text: September 08, 2025 9:50 AM by Tennant Company Posted in Best Practices , Industry News & Trends , Cleaning Challenges , An overview of floor scrubber squeegees and maintenance best practices By rotating the squeegee blade, you can clean with all four sides of it – increasing the life of the squeegee. Squeegee Blade Overview What is a squeegee? Other than being a funny word, the squeegee is arguably one of the most important components of a floor scrubber. In the simplest terms, a squeegee blade is a piece of rubber, urethane, Linatex®, or Primothane® that attaches to the back and/or sides of a floor scrubber or sweeper-scrubber and funnels water so the vacuum fan can pick up the liquid as the floor cleaning machine passes over it. The combination of the squeegee assembly, squeegee blades and vacuum fan allows for optimal water pick-up. The squeegee is a critical component of the machine’s water management system, which leaves floors clean, and even more importantly, dry and safe, which helps to prevent slip-and-fall accidents — one of the most frequent types of worker compensation claims, according to the EHS Daily Advisor. If your squeegee blades are not properly maintained, your floor scrubber may leave behind streaks, debris or water, resulting in rework and wasted time, which costs you extra money. EVERY 30 MINUTES OF EXTRA CLEANING = $259 EXTRA LABOR COSTS PER MONTH, OR $3,151 ANNUALLY* Squeegee Blade Materials There are multiple materials that floor cleaning squeegees can be made of, such as rubber and urethane, and each material has qualities that make it ideal for certain types of floors or environments. Download our Squeegee Material Guide Linatex® squeegees are a premium blade material and come standard on most Tennant equipment. The proprietary material offers outstanding strength, resilience and resistance for long-lasting performance. Linatex is ideal for wet applications when paired with a Linard® squeegee for the front blade. Primothane® squeegees are oil-resistant and flexible, with strong dry abrasion resistance for longer life. They provide optimal water pick-up on rubber and epoxy anti-slip floors. Urethane squeegees are chemical resistant, making them ideal for cleaning organic and petroleum-based oils. Gum rubber squeegee blades are the lowest cost, which helps you save money on replacements. These squeegees are slightly stiffer and are recommended for smooth and even indoor floors. Gum rubber is not chemical resistant. Floor scrubbers have squeegee blades on the back, and sometimes sides, to help funnel water and cleaning solution so the vacuum fan can suck them up as it cleans, leaving your floor clean and dry. Squeegees are available in a variety of materials to best match the facility’s floor type and environment. Squeegee Blade Replacement and Maintenance While squeegees may be one of the most commonly replaced parts on your floor cleaning equipment, there are many things you can do to keep them in optimal condition for as long as possible to cut down on replacement costs. Rotate squeegees for increased life. By rotating which side of the squeegee is on the floor, you can get longer use out of a single blade. Squeegee wear depends on the material of the squeegee and the type and condition of the floor. Inspect the condition of your squeegee blades daily and rotate or replace the blade when it is worn halfway through. Clean and store squeegees properly. Rinse down the squeegee assembly after use to prevent buildup and always store blades off the floor. This simple step helps extend blade life and ensures consistent cleaning performance. Replace squeegees before they become ineffective. When you begin to see wear and tear on an edge of your squeegee blade, rotate it in a timely manner, and once cleaning on the 4th edge, have a replacement blade ready to go so you’re always cleaning with a highly performing squeegee and not sacrificing cleanliness and safety. Purchase OEM squeegees for optimal performance. Look-alike or third party squeegees blades are not specifically designed for your cleaning machine and may not provide the quality of cleaning you expect. While the squeegees blades may look the same, don’t be fooled by lower priced parts – you will spend more in the long run replacing poorly made squeegees than purchasing OEM squeegees. When a squeegee is worn halfway through, rotate it to a new side to maintain optimal performance. Ensure there is even pressure across the entire squeegee blade. A properly positioned squeegee has even pressure from tip to tip and is set on the floor at an angle where the inside edge of the squeegee blade is scraping across the floor for optimal water pick-up. If there is too much pressure, the squeegee can get smashed down and will not pick up water properly. Download our Squeegee User Guide How To Resolve Common Squeegee Issues: Squeegee is not picking up water in the center. Adjustments to the amount of pressure on the squeegee blade can be made to ensure there is equal distribution across the entire length, which will prevent the center of the blade from being higher than the tips. Review your operator manual to understand how to best adjust the squeegees on your machine. Squeegee is not picking up water on the edges. Similar to the example above, there may be adjustments that need to be made to ensure the squeegee is dragging across the floor at the correct angle. Review your operator manual to understand how to best adjust the squeegees on your machine. Streaks are being left on the floor. In this case, it’s likely your squeegee blade has dirt or debris built up on it, which is causing the squeegee to inconsistently drag across the floor. To resolve, raise your squeegee assembly and wipe the length of your squeegees with a clean rag or towel to remove the debris. By choosing the right squeegee blade for your environment and properly maintaining them, you will save money and time in replacement costs and rework. Need help selecting the right squeegee for your machine? Read our Squeegee Material Guide . *Based on using a 32-inch rider scrubber on 150,000 square feet of cleanable space. Assumes $17.27 per hour wage (According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, May 2024, Median Hourly Wage) and 30 days of cleaning per month.
